description:
From the 2026-07-12 tuning review, finding R7 (evidence pinned to commit
acfb8992). 467 tuning unit tests pass while every soundness boundary has zero
coverage:

- No test covers requested-vs-applied integrity (tunings_applied vs executed
  statements).
- Validation-status tests pin "PASSED" (test_tpc_tuning_template_parity.py:231,270),
  a value production never emits (real set: NOT_APPLICABLE/APPLIED/
  FAILED_TO_SAVE/NOT_VALIDATED).
- No test calls get_ddl_generator at all; no registry-completeness test.
- No cross-consistency test across the capability sources (interface compat
  map, generator registry, platform_capabilities mapping).
- No tests for hash stability/canonicality (get_configuration_hash,
  hash_tuning_template).
- No shared Python<->TypeScript tuning_mode vocabulary pin; Python emits
  "balanced" (cli/tuning.py:52,56) unknown to the explorer.
- Resolver's emitted fallback log marker and coverage.py's parser expectation
  can drift silently (coverage tests hand-write the strings).

anti_patterns.dont: No tests that merely mirror implementation constants
anti_patterns.why: each must encode an invariant that catches drift

deferrals.reason: Ledger shape gated on ADR-1; w6 pins today's requested-side behavior first
deferrals.resolved_reason: [G4 sweep] duplicate: Full applied-ledger integrity assertions are covered by open item tuning-applied-ledger-and-validation-status-20260712 (applied-tuning ledger + honest validation_status).

preserves.behavior: Existing 467 passing tuning tests (modify only the fictional-vocabulary fixtures)

prior_art.concept: benchbox/core/results/schema_specs.yaml + benchmark_specs.yaml: existing YAML-spec-consumed-by-code pattern — reuse for the shared tuning_mode vocabulary pin
tests/uat/data/tuning_coverage.tsv: existing checked-in matrix asserted by tests — same enforcement shape

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m pytest tests/unit/core/tuning tests/unit/cli/test_tuning* -q
verifications.description: New suites pass and fail-on-drift is demonstrated (mutate one registry entry locally, observe failure, revert)
verifications.expected: All passing; drift-demo documented in PR body

work_units.notes:
Replaced both "PASSED" fixtures in test_tpc_tuning_template_parity.py
(lines 231, 270) with "APPLIED" (a value adapter.py actually emits).
Added tests/unit/core/tuning/test_validation_status_vocabulary.py,
which statically extracts every string literal adapter.py assigns to
`tuning_validation_status` via `ast` (not a hand-copied set) plus the
BenchmarkResults dataclass default, and pins the union against
{NOT_APPLICABLE, APPLIED, FAILED_TO_SAVE, NOT_VALIDATED}.
work_units.summary: Pin the real validation-status vocabulary in tests; remove fictional 'PASSED' fixtures

work_units.notes:
tests/unit/core/tuning/test_hash_canonicality.py covers both
BenchmarkTunings.get_configuration_hash (insertion-order stability,
distinctness, full 64-char sha256 hexdigest -- NOT truncated) and
profile_validation.hash_tuning_template (same properties, but
confirmed truncated to 16 hex chars/64 bits). The 16-char truncation's
collision posture (non-negligible birthday-bound collisions past
~2**32 configs; not a cryptographic identity proof on its own) is
documented directly in that test's assertion message.
work_units.summary: Hash canonicality tests: dict-ordering stability, semantic-equivalence, distinctness across differing configs, truncation posture documented

work_units.notes:
Narrowed per the orchestrator's guidance: PR #1174 already landed a
sync test between _PLATFORM_COMPATIBILITY_MAP and
_KNOWN_COMPATIBILITY_PLATFORMS (test_platform_identity_keys.py) --
those two literally cannot diverge (one is derived from the other), so
this TODO does not duplicate it. tests/unit/core/tuning/
test_capability_source_drift.py instead covers the two sources #1174
didn't touch: get_ddl_generator()'s registry (keys extracted via `ast`
from its own dict literal, not re-declared) vs _PLATFORM_COMPATIBILITY_MAP,
and platform_capabilities.map_candidate_to_platform's empirically-
probed supported set (by calling the real function across every
WorkloadTuningCandidate role, not re-implementing its branch logic) vs
_PLATFORM_COMPATIBILITY_MAP. Every current divergence is enumerated in
an EXPECTED_* allowlist with a reason (ADR-3 gates consolidation);
exact-match assertions against those allowlists fail on both new drift
and stale (over-broad) allowlist entries, mirroring
test_ddl_generator_registry.py's stale-exemption check. Drift-demo:
temporarily removed the "mysql" entry from
_PLATFORM_COMPATIBILITY_MAP in interface.py -- 2 of the 6 new tests
failed with clear stale-allowlist messages naming "mysql"; reverted via
the pre-edit backup and the suite returned to green (see PR body / this
completion note; no diff left in interface.py).
work_units.summary: Cross-source consistency test over capability registries (expected-drift allowlist so it fails only on NEW drift until consolidation lands)

work_units.notes:
tests/unit/cli/test_tuning_marker_coverage_roundtrip.py calls the real
resolve_tuning() (notuning / tuned-fallback-no-template / tuned-
fallback-no-platform-benchmark / tuned-auto-discovered / auto /
explicit-file) and feeds its actual TuningResolution.info_messages
straight into coverage.py's real status_from_log_text() -- no marker
substrings are hand-written in the test. No changes to coverage.py
were needed; status_from_log_text and the three status constants were
already public/importable.
work_units.summary: Resolver marker <-> coverage.py parser round-trip test (resolver emits, parser classifies; no hand-written strings)

work_units.notes:
Shared artifact: tests/unit/core/tuning/fixtures/tuning_mode_vocabulary.yaml
(NOT under a `data/` directory -- the repo .gitignore blanket-ignores
those; caught this via `git status` showing the file untracked/`!!`
after the first write and relocated it). Pins ADR-2's decided set
{tuned, tuned-fallback, notuning, auto, custom} plus the
not-recorded sentinel as a TEST CONTRACT, not current-emitter
compliance (cli/tuning.py still emits "balanced";
TuningBadge.tsx/TUNING_CONFIG still only knows tuned/notuning/auto --
migrating those is the separate, unstarted
tuning-mode-vocabulary-and-facet-implementation-20260712).
tests/unit/core/tuning/test_tuning_mode_vocabulary.py (Python) and
results-explorer/src/lib/__tests__/tuningModeVocabulary.test.ts
(TypeScript) both assert directly against that same YAML file: the TS
test loads it via a `uv run -- python -c` subprocess, the same
shell-out pattern already established by db-remediation-pin.test.ts,
rather than maintaining a separate hardcoded TS mirror that would need
its own regex-based cross-check. This satisfies ADR-2 §2's "single
shared artifact" requirement more directly than the originally-sketched
TS-constants-plus-regex-parse fallback.
work_units.summary: Shared vocabulary pin: single source (JSON/YAML) asserted by both pytest and vitest for tuning_mode values

work_units.notes:
tests/unit/core/tuning/test_requested_vs_applied_capture.py builds a
stub PlatformAdapter (tuning_enabled=True) whose apply_unified_tuning
deliberately executes only a constraint statement against a recording
connection, skipping every requested table-level tuning (simulating a
silent partial-application). Calling the real
_setup_fresh_database_phases and reproducing adapter.py's real
run_enhanced_benchmark derivation (tunings_applied_dict =
effective_tuning_config.to_dict(); tuning_validation_status = "APPLIED"
if tuning_metadata_saved else "FAILED_TO_SAVE") shows the documented
gap: tunings_applied still lists both tables' sort tunings even though
the connection only ever saw one statement, and
tuning_validation_status="APPLIED" reflects only that the metadata row
was saved. Named and documented explicitly as pinning requested-config
capture, not applied verification, per the applied-ledger deferral
below.
work_units.summary: Requested-vs-applied harness: adapter-level test with a recording connection asserting executed tuning statements are reflected in captured metadata (deepens once the applied ledger lands)
